nodes.statement: State precisely the upper and lower estimates obtained, their quantifiers, and every constant's dependence on r. A subexponential-factor or exponent-level determination counts only if it genuinely answers the open-ended 'Estimate f_r(N)' request rather than merely restating a known one-sided record.
Any advertised uniform-in-r conclusion is proved with constants independent of N; a theorem for one fixed r is labeled only a fixed-r result.
DETERMINATION CLOSE: give a rigorous asymptotic estimate for f_r(N) in the sense claimed, uniformly for every fixed r≥3; an exact or sharper theorem is acceptable if it implies the stated estimate.
A refutation names the precise proposed estimate it refutes and supplies a theorem determining the contrary growth behavior; merely failing an auxiliary conjecture is not a classification of f_r.

ALTERNATIVE DETERMINATION CLOSE: provide a complete mathematically decisive outcome incompatible with the proposed estimate, or a genuine independence theorem for the exact estimation proposition being claimed.

Let $r\geq 3$, and let $f_r(N)$ denote the size of the largest subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that no subset of size $r$ has the same pairwise greatest common divisor between all elements. Estimate $f_r(N)$.
